definitions.def: to judge the value, amount, or quality of something
not aware of or controlled by your conscious mind
to give a good reason for something
completely sure that something is true

grammar_choice.en_template: We go out in the world every day and {{1:make/makes}} decisions about {{2:what/that}} is safe or not and what is appropriate or not.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 우리는 매일 세상에 나가 무엇이 안전한지 아닌지, 무엇이 적절한지 아닌지에 대해 결정을 내린다.
explain: 주어 We(복수) + 등위 동사 → 원형 make.
about의 목적어가 되는 간접의문문(명사절)의 주어 → 의문사 what.

grammar_choice.en_template: It is what psychologist Joseph LeDoux has suggested is an unconscious "danger detector" that {{1:determines/determine}} whether or not something or someone is safe before we can even begin to {{2:consciously make/make consciously}} a determination.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 심리학자 Joseph LeDoux가 제안한 바에 따르면, 우리가 의식적으로 판단을 내리기 시작하기도 전에 어떤 것이나 누군가가 안전한지 아닌지를 결정하는 것은 무의식적인 "위험 감지기"이다.
explain: It is ~ that 강조구문 — 강조 대상(danger detector, 단수)에 수일치 → determines.
to부정사 사이에 부사 삽입(분리부정사) consciously make — 원문 어순.

grammar_choice.en_template: When the object, animal, or person {{1:is assessed/assesses}} to be dangerous, a fear response, {{2:which/what}} has been called "fight or flight," occurs.

grammar_choice.en_template: On a conscious level we may correct a mistake in this "danger detector" when we notice it, but often, of course, we simply begin to generate reasons for {{1:why/which}} it was {{2:accurate/accurately}} in the first place.

grammar_choice.en_template: We are generally convinced {{1:that/what}} our decisions are "rational," but in reality, most human decisions are {{2:made/making}} emotionally, and then we collect or generate the facts to justify these decisions.

jumble.answer: We go out in the world every day and make decisions about what is safe or not and what is appropriate or not.

It is what psychologist Joseph LeDoux has suggested is an unconscious "danger detector" that determines whether or not something or someone is safe before we can even begin to consciously make a determination.
When the object, animal, or person is assessed to be dangerous, a fear response, which has been called "fight or flight," occurs.
On a conscious level we may correct a mistake in this "danger detector" when we notice it, but often, of course, we simply begin to generate reasons for why it was accurate in the first place.
We are generally convinced that our decisions are "rational," but in reality, most human decisions are made emotionally, and then we collect or generate the facts to justify these decisions.
When we see something or someone who "feels" dangerous, we have already launched into action internally before we have even started "thinking."
